threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will come on time—try catching the 38 at peak and you'll learn quickly. It's more of a suggestion, not a schedule.
Saw a guy in a bright pink onesie doing karaoke on the 59 last night, and no one even flinched. Just another Saturday in Brixton, I guess.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the sound of U-Bahn construction at dawn became a lullaby, blending with the smell of fresh Döner wafting from the corner shop.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar that opens at 8 AM for game days—pints of beer alongside currywurst before the first whistle.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they still call it the 'BART' and not 'the train'—that love for the broken system runs deep.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy pull a full-on yoga routine in the back of a packed Muni bus. Everyone just awkwardly pretended it was normal. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars have tapas at the same time, but locals know it's all about the after-work pintxos at 8, not at 10.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still trying to navigate the tram system without a T10 card, peering at Google Maps like it’s a puzzle that doesn’t match.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look at the bus stop timetable like it means something, instead of just setting your watch to 'eventually'.
Caught the 196 last night, and there was a guy reciting Shakespeare to a bemused crowd. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The way the kebab shop owner knows your order without you saying a word. That's when it hit me—it's more than just a place, it's home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop that proudly displays its 'Best Currywurst' award in the window—right next to the doner meat. It’s a delicious identity crisis.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a true local when they can navigate the BART delays and still manage to make it to La Taqueria for a burrito, no matter what.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: I watched a guy serenade the bus with a ukulele today; his best audience was a couple of pigeons perched on the stop sign.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the local bars serve only tapas, but the best are the unmarked ones that just do vermut on tap, no frills.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll notice them standing at every crosswalk, waiting for the light to change even when no cars are in sight.
